notes:
User is cleaning and organizing their garage this weekend. Their main clutter categories are tools and sports equipment, and they plan to remove old furniture, especially a long-unused dusty desk, by donating/selling or responsibly disposing of it. Cleared space will become a dedicated cleaning workstation, replacing work done on the kitchen counter, for all-purpose cleaners, disinfectant, dusters, paper towels, a cordless vacuum, and a microfiber mop. They plan to use the “one-touch rule” during the purge and a Keep/Donate or Sell/Discard system, with a “maybe” box and review deadline if needed. Storage will use stackable bins, shelving/hooks, and clear, consistent labels; frequent-use items will be easiest to access. They chose a Brother P-Touch label maker and may use a color-coded system.

User also plans to organize a bookshelf by purging unwanted books, grouping similar books by category, using shelf rather than book labels, and possibly adding a to-read section.

For cleaning supplies, they are deciding between organizing by room or product type. A practical hybrid was suggested: organize primarily by product type, then subdivide by room when useful. Supplies should be clear
